macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures point higher as markets recover from AI selloff
items.summary: U.S. stock futures rose Monday, with Dow futures up about 1.0%, S&P 500 futures up 0.7%, and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.7% before the open. Investors were attempting to stabilize after last week’s sharp technology and AI-related losses.[5]

items.title: Strong jobs report increases expectations for December Fed hike
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above forecasts, while unemployment fell to 4.1%. Markets priced in nearly an 80% chance of at least a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, with officials emphasizing that inflation remains above the 2% goal.[2]

items.title: U.S. inflation data becomes the week’s key market catalyst
items.summary: Investors are awaiting Tuesday’s consumer-price index report for further evidence about the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path; producer-price data is due later in the week. Strong inflation could reinforce expectations for another rate increase.[1]

items.title: Nvidia falls on reported investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell about 5% premarket after reports that the company was investigating whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The development added volatility to an already fragile AI trade.[5]

items.title: Asian markets stabilize as chip stocks rebound
items.summary: Asian equities and U.S. futures steadied after a volatile week, as concerns about AI demand and tighter regulation eased somewhat. Upcoming earnings from CoreWeave, Applied Materials, and Cisco are expected to provide fresh signals on AI infrastructure spending.[2]

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway reports lower operating earnings
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway reported a 5.8% year-over-year decline in third-quarter operating earnings, primarily reflecting weaker insurance results. Class B shares were modestly lower in premarket trading.[1]

items.title: KKR and Constellation Energy report strong quarterly results
items.summary: KKR rose after reporting record quarterly profit, while Constellation Energy gained after adjusted third-quarter earnings exceeded expectations. Both companies were among notable premarket movers.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $74,000 as crypto sell-off intensifies
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $73,962, down 2.77% intraday, while broader cryptocurrency declines were accompanied by heavy derivatives liquidations.[3]

items.title: Ethereum drops more than 4% amid $462 million in liquidations
items.summary: Ether fell more than 4% over 24 hours as leveraged long positions were liquidated and institutional fund withdrawals added selling pressure.[1]

items.title: U.S. Treasury sanctions eight Canadian money-service companies
items.summary: The Treasury Department imposed sanctions on eight Canadian money-service businesses it said had conducted transactions involving sanctioned Iranian entities.[6]

items.title: FinCEN action against MEXC triggers withdrawal concerns
items.summary: Users reported delays and reviews involving withdrawals from MEXC after FinCEN issued a special-measures order; the order had not officially taken effect, and the scope of restrictions remained unclear.[8]

items.title: Binance France to close operations
items.summary: Binance France reportedly plans to close all user accounts in the country on December 31.[6]

items.title: Zcash developers consider another block-time reduction
items.summary: Zcash developers are seeking a further reduction in block times shortly after the NU7 upgrade reduced the interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.[6]

items.title: Raycash launches privacy-focused stablecoin project on Ethereum
items.summary: Raycash, a project spun off from privacy protocol Zama, launched on Ethereum mainnet with privacy-focused stablecoin payments and yield features; it is currently in private beta.[3]

items.title: Progmat and Digital Asset plan blockchain settlement for Japanese assets
items.summary: Japan’s Progmat signed an agreement with Digital Asset Holdings to explore migrating trading and settlement of real-world assets, including Japanese government bonds, to the Canton Network.[3]

items.title: ACryptoS halts operations after $665,000 vault attack
items.summary: DeFi yield aggregator ACryptoS reported a vault exploit causing approximately $665,000 in losses, disabled deposits, and urged users to withdraw remaining funds.[9]

items.title: Ethereum delays Hoodi testnet fork over contract risks
items.summary: Ethereum developers will not fork the Hoodi testnet for the Glamsterdam upgrade until contract risks identified by ChainSecurity are resolved.[7]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Football Manager 27 launches November 10
items.summary: Sports Interactive’s Football Manager 27 is scheduled to launch on November 10, with the latest coverage highlighting its release as one of the week’s major gaming events.

items.title: Gen.G reaches League of Legends Worlds final
items.summary: Gen.G defeated Invictus Gaming 3–0 in the 2026 League of Legends World Championship semifinals. T1 lost 3–1 to Bilibili Gaming, ending its bid for a fourth consecutive title.

items.title: Dreadmoor launches on November 9
items.summary: The post-apocalyptic fishing and survival adventure Dreadmoor launches on November 9, combining boat exploration, crafting, trading, combat, and mutated-creature encounters.

items.title: Publisher blames AI-related Steam review backlog for delayed launch
items.summary: The co-op game Wheel Make It reportedly launched weeks late after an approval delay, resulting in a peak of only 15 concurrent players despite more than 11,000 wishlists. Its publisher attributed the delay to an alleged backlog linked to the volume of AI-assisted games submitted to Steam.

items.title: HoYoverse returns to G-STAR with two titles
items.summary: HoYoverse is attending South Korea’s G-STAR for the first time in four years and plans to gather local user feedback on two upcoming titles.

items.title: Skydance reportedly cuts video-game staff
items.summary: Skydance reportedly laid off an unspecified number of employees in its video-game divisions following Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros.

items.title: GTA VI physical edition reportedly requires a download code
items.summary: Reports say boxed copies of Grand Theft Auto VI will contain a download code rather than a game disc, with the installation expected to require up to 212 GB of storage.
